title: ‘Paradise Lost’ From ‘Train to Busan’ Director Yeon Sang-ho Acquired by Well Go USA Entertainment (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Paradise Lost,” the latest mystery-thriller from “Train to Busan” and “Hellbound” filmmaker Yeon Sang-ho, has been bought by Well Go USA Entertainm
body:
“Paradise Lost,” the latest mystery-thriller from “Train to Busan” and “Hellbound” filmmaker Yeon Sang-ho, has been bought by Well Go USA Entertainment ahead of its world premiere at Toronto. 

	“Paradise Lost” will bow Sept. 13 at Toronto’s Royal Alexandra Theatre as part of TIFF’s Special Presentations lineup, marking Yeon’s fourth appearance at the festival.

	Starring Kim Hyun-joo and Bae Hyeon-seong, the film follows a mother whose young son mysteriously disappears along with a bus full of children. Years later, he unexpectedly returns — but has changed in ways she could never have imagined.
	

	“I am thrilled to present ‘Paradise Lost’ to North American audiences through Well Go USA,” Yeon said. “‘Paradise Lost’ is a psychological thriller that dives deep into the abyss of a mother, caught between the son she resurrected in a virtual world through AI and the son who returns after being presumed dead.”


	“Even though ‘Colony’ and ‘Paradise Lost’ are entirely different in the way they present fear and entertainment, I hope North American audiences are able to enjoy both,” the director continued. 

	The acquisition continues Well Go USA’s longstanding relationship with Yeon, having previously handled his zombie blockbuster “Train to Busan,” as well as “The Ugly” and “Colony.”

	“Audiences are in for a haunting, emotionally resonant experience, and we’re proud to introduce the film to U.S. audiences following its world premiere at TIFF,” said Well Go USA president and CEO Doris Pfardrescher, who described “Paradise Lost“ as a “gripping and deeply human mystery that showcases his singular ability to find terror in the most intimate places.” 
	

	Yeon broke out internationally with 2016’s “Train to Busan,” which premiered at Cannes and became a global hit, and has since expanded across film and television with projects including Netflix supernatural series “Hellbound.”

	Well Go USA plans to release “Paradise Lost” in the U.S. following its TIFF premiere.

schema.headline: ‘Paradise Lost’ From ‘Train to Busan’ Director Yeon Sang-ho Acquired by Well Go USA Entertainment (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Joko Anwar’s ‘Satan’s Slaves: Origin’ Boarded by Barunson E&A for International Sales
description: Joko Anwar‘s “Satan’s Slaves: Origin” (original title: “Pengabdi Setan 3: Origin”), the next chapter in the filmmaker’s blockbuster horror franchise
body:
Joko Anwar‘s “Satan’s Slaves: Origin” (original title: “Pengabdi Setan 3: Origin”), the next chapter in the filmmaker’s blockbuster horror franchise, has been boarded for worldwide sales by Barunson E&A, the Korean studio behind Bong Joon Ho’s Oscar-winning “Parasite.” 

	The company will launch the project to international buyers at the Toronto Film Festival‘s inaugural market this September.


	Though it’s the third film in the franchise, “Satan’s Slaves: Origin” stands alone as a prequel, tracing the cult and demonic pact behind the first two movies back to their source. The story opens with an outbreak of mass hysteria in 16th-century Strasbourg, drawing on a real incident recorded in 1518, then jumps to a haunted lighthouse on Java’s southern coast in the 17th century. It’s the most ambitious production of Anwar’s career to date, spanning two continents and filmed in seven languages – Indonesian, Alsatian, Portuguese, Javanese, Dutch, Turkish and Latin.
	

	“This film is everything I didn’t know I was building toward – the one that finally answers where the curse came from, why it never stopped, and what it’s really after,” Anwar said. “Longtime fans are going to get the answers they’ve waited years for. Newcomers are going to get the ride of their lives.”


	Rapi Films is producing, with Anwar writing and directing and Come and See Pictures, Sky Media and Legacy Pictures co-producing. The film is in pre-production, targeting a 2027 theatrical release in Indonesia.

	The “Satan’s Slaves” name carries weight in Indonesia: Rapi Films’ original 1980 version is a local cult classic, Anwar’s 2017 revival topped the year’s local box office and is credited with jump-starting the country’s current horror boom, and 2022’s “Satan’s Slaves: Communion” became the first Indonesian film to play in Imax and remains among the six highest-grossing local releases ever.
	

	The deal extends an existing two-year exclusive partnership between Anwar and Barunson E&A, whose last collaboration, “Ghost in the Cell,” currently sits at No. 2 on Indonesia’s local box office chart for the year. That horror-comedy bowed at the Berlin Film Festival and has since pulled in over 3.3 million local admissions and sold to 150 territories, with Plaion taking Germany and Well Go USA taking North America.

	Choi Yoonhee, CEO of Barunson E&A, said, “Every time we work with Joko Anwar, the scale gets bigger and the ambition gets sharper. ‘Satan’s Slaves: Origin’ is unlike anything he’s made – a story that moves across centuries and continents. It’s proof of what we’ve believed for years: Indonesian filmmakers are telling some of the boldest genre stories in the world right now, and we’re proud to help this one reach it.”

	It’s the latest in a run of Asian genre pickups for Barunson E&A, which has also boarded Banjong Pisanthanakun’s “Inherit,” the Indonesian zombie thriller “Zona Merah: Dead City” and the Korean occult title “Stoneborn,” from the makers of “Exhuma.”

schema.headline: Joko Anwar’s ‘Satan’s Slaves: Origin’ Boarded by Barunson E&A for International Sales

title: ‘Big Mistakes’ Season 2 Casts Lorenzo de Moor, Poorna Jagannathan
description:
“Big Mistakes” Season 2 is now in production, with the Netflix comedy series adding two actors in recurring roles. 

	Both Lorenzo de Moor and Poorn
body:
“Big Mistakes” Season 2 is now in production, with the Netflix comedy series adding two actors in recurring roles. 

	Both Lorenzo de Moor and Poorna Jagannathan will recur in the show’s second season, joining returning stars Dan Levy, Taylor Ortega, Laurie Metcalf, Jack Innanen, Boran Kuzum and Abby Quinn. As previously announced, Elizabeth Perkins has been upped to series regular status for Season 2. 


	de Moor will play Leo, while Jagannathan will play Dréa. Exact character details are being kept under wraps. 
	

	de Moor has starred in Italian films like “Dolce Fine Giornata” and American releases like “Another Simple Favor” and “You, Me & Tuscany.” Next up, he will be seen in features including “The Resurrection of the Christ: Part One,” the reboot of “Cliffhanger,” and “Maserati: The Brothers.” 

	Jagannathan currently stars in the HBO-DC Studios series “Lanterns” and is fresh off her role as Lucky in the critically-acclaimed Hulu comedy “Deli Boys.” She previously starred in the Netflix series “Never Have I Ever” and has been in shows like “The Night Of” at HBO and “Better Call Saul.” In film, she is known for roles in “Delhi Belly,” “Wolfs,” and “Turtles All the Way Down.” 

	de Moor is repped by Volver Consulenze Artistiche and 42. Jagannathan is repped by Gersh, Untitled, and Hansen Jacobson. 

	The official logline for Season 1 of “Big Mistakes” states that it “follows Nicky (Levy) and Morgan (Ortega), two deeply incapable siblings who are in over their heads when a misguided theft for their dying grandmother accidentally pulls them into the world of organized crime. Blackmailed into increasingly dangerous assignments, they clumsily fail upwards, sinking deeper into chaos they’re ill-equipped to handle.” 
	

	Levy created the series and serves as executive producer and showrunner in addition to starring. Rachel Sennott also co-created the series and executive produces. Anne-Marie McGintee executive produces for Not a Real Production Company, with Jacqui Rivera and Timothy Greenberg also executive producing.

title: D4vd Abruptly Parts Ways With Legal Team in Favor of Public Defenders
description: Singer D4vd has parted ways with his legal representation in favor of public defenders for his case in which he is accused of allegedly killing and
body:
Singer D4vd has parted ways with his legal representation in favor of public defenders for his case in which he is accused of allegedly killing and dismembering a 14-year-old girl.

	The singer, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, appeared in a Los Angeles court earlier this morning and asked to have the public defender’s office replace his legal team, which represented Harvey Weinstein and L.A. labor union leader David Huerta. According to the LA Times, Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Charlaine Olmedo granted his request and held a closed meeting with his attorneys
	

	Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski and Regina Peter shared in a joint statement that they were parting ways with their client after the court granted the request. “We continue to support David and his defense against these serious charges,” reads the statement. “We are grateful that the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office has taken over the representation and that David has a highly capable and committed team of attorneys and investigators behind him.”


	Burke’s appearance in court on Monday was a post-preliminary hearing where he pleaded not guilty to the charges against him, which include a first-degree murder charge that could potentially make him eligible for the death penalty. He will also face charges for lewd acts with a child and for dismembering the girl’s body.

	In July, Burke was ordered to stand trial after prosecutors presented evidence that connected him to the murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez. He was arrested on April 16 in Los Angeles and charged days later. Prosecutors alleged that Burke had murdered Hernandez after she threatened to expose their relationship and ruin his career.
	

	The next hearing for Burke will take place on October 19.

schema.headline: D4vd Abruptly Parts Ways With Legal Team in Favor of Public Defenders

title: Mel Gibson Apologizes for Mocking Sign Language Interpreter at Backlash Grows: ‘Thoughtless Idiocy’ With ‘No Intended Maliciousness’
description: Mel Gibson has issued an apology amid backlash over his recent appearance at FanExpo Canada, where the Oscar winner mocked an ASL interpreter while
body:
Mel Gibson has issued an apology amid backlash over his recent appearance at FanExpo Canada, where the Oscar winner mocked an ASL interpreter while walking on stage to attend his retrospective Q&A. Video of the incident was widely circulated on social media platforms like X, with Gibson condemned for his insensitive actions. 

	“Sometimes when you get pushed out on a stage in a spotlight your mind is all over the place, and sometimes spontaneous thoughtless idiocy is displayed,” Gibson said in a statement to Variety. “There was no intended maliciousness attached, and I certainly apologize to anyone who was upset by it.”
	

	Variety has reached out to representatives for FanExpo Canada for additional comment.


	FanExpo Canada is held annually and is billed as “the largest comics, sci-fi, horror, anime and gaming event in Canada and the third-largest Pop Culture event in North America.” Gibson’s appearance at this year’s expo took place Saturday, Aug. 29, and included autograph and photo opportunities for fans that were priced at $275 each, per the event’s website.

	The viral video of Gibson appearing to mock the Fan Expo ASL interpreter sparked backlash against the actor as well as FanExpo for platforming the controversial star. Users on X also began sharing a video of “Reacher” star Alan Ritchson at the same event and praising him for shaking the hand of the ASL interpreter after his Q&A wrapped.

	Gibson, who recently wrapped production on his “Passion of the Christ” follow-up movie “The Resurrection of the Christ,” has been on the expo circuit this summer. He previously attended Fan Expo Boston, where he made headlines for touting why “Lethal Weapon 5” never happened.
	

	Gibson was infamously arrested in 2006, during which he made disparaging comments about Jewish people. The backlash against Gibson over his antisemitic remarks soured his career in Hollywood. The upcoming two-part “Passion of the Christ” follow-up could mark his return to box office domination considering the 2004 original earned $612 million worldwide and was the highest-grossing R-rated movie for nearly two decades.

schema.headline: Mel Gibson Apologizes for Mocking Sign Language Interpreter at Backlash Grows: ‘Thoughtless Idiocy’ With ‘No Intended Maliciousness’

title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Smashes Record for Most Weeks at No. 1 for a Non-Holiday Song
description: Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” has topped 20 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — making it the longest run ever at the top of the chart for a
body:
Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” has topped 20 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — making it the longest run ever at the top of the chart for a non-holiday song.

	The song passed Shaboozey’s 2024 hit “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” and “Old Town Road,” by Lil Nas X feat. Billy Ray Cyrus, with which it was tied for a 19-week run — and if it holds on for three more weeks, it will pass Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” which holds the record with 22 weeks over the past seven years.
	

	If “Choosin’ Texas” manages to go the distance and somehow beat “All I Want for Christmas” as the all-time leader in weeks at No. 1, it may be a short-lived victory, of course, since the Carey song has tended to go No. 1 for a few weeks every December in recent years. 


	Langley’s hit has been certified six-times platinum, with more likely to come. She swept all seven of her nominations at the 2026 ACM Awards, setting a new record for the most wins by an artist in a single year, including female artist of the year and song and single of the year for “Choosin’ Texas.” She followed that with two American Music Awards, for best female country artist and best country song. And the victory lap isn’t over: “Choosin’ Texas” was just nominated for best country at the 2026 MTV VMAs. 

	The singer recently launched the second leg of her sold-out “Dandelion” tour, which continues through the fall with upcoming stops including Red Rocks Amphitheatre and two nights at The Greek Theatre in Los Angeles.

schema.headline: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Smashes Record for Most Weeks at No. 1 for a Non-Holiday Song

title: Hollywood Assistant Horror Novel ‘This Town Will Eat You Alive’ Written Under Pseudonym by Industry Insider Set at Hanover Square Press (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
A satirical Hollywood horror-romance novel is set to release next year from Hanover Square Press and debut author Clare Ogawa. 

	The book, titled “
body:
A satirical Hollywood horror-romance novel is set to release next year from Hanover Square Press and debut author Clare Ogawa. 

	The book, titled “This Town Will Eat you Alive,” follows an assistant who learns the movie exec she works for is turning into a tentacled monster that eats women alive. While obviously fictitious, the work is based on Ogawa’s own experiences as an assistant in show biz and Ogawa is writing under a pseudonym in order to maintain her anonymity while she’s still working within the industry.
	

	Releasing July 6, 2027, “This Town Will Eat You Alive” follows Frankie Meyers, who has one goal: To claw her way to the top of Hollywood and become an Oscar-winning producer. But for now, she’s stuck as the assistant to Lee Becker, famous studio head and infamously horrible boss.


	Per the book’s synopsis, “Frankie is willing to endure Lee’s angry rants and impossible requests because he’s her golden ticket to the top — but her ambitions are derailed when she discovers that girls are going missing around him.  Everyone knows about Lee’s reputation, but her digging uncovers something far worse than the usual Hollywood misogyny. Lee Becker is transforming into something monstrous and tentacled at night. Something with a voracious appetite for blondes. Frankie figures she’s probably safe since she’s half-Japanese and not his usual type, but she still needs to stop him. And when his son, Blue Becker, also learns the truth, she’s happy to have help from someone who believes that there’s something left of Lee to save. But when girls continue to disappear despite their efforts, Frankie and Blue must choose between their own desires and stopping the monster for good.”
	

	The North American rights to the book were acquired by Hanover Square Press’s Dina Davis in a preempt from Jenny Bent at her eponymous agency.

	Hanover Square Press provided the following bio for the pen-name author behind “This Town Will Eat You Alive”: Clare Ogawa is a Gen-Z mixed Japanese-American author. She currently lives in Los Angeles, where by day, she works in Hollywood. While not quite as absurd or grisly as the events in ‘This Town Will Eat You Alive,’ her personal experiences starting as an assistant and working her way up to executive in the weird and wonderful film industry inspired this horror novel.

	“Like a lot of young people, I only started working in the industry after the #MeToo movement, and I had no idea what to expect,” Ogawa said. “What sort of behavior was labeled acceptable or not anymore? What if someone escaped the movement when they shouldn’t have? Would they actually change their behavior, or would they just hide it better? Making the boss a literal monster was a way to externalize all of those fears. It also provides an interesting conundrum for a young female protagonist entering an industry with full knowledge of its fraught history. There’s a tension between knowing what’s already been exposed, the aspiration of what the industry should be, and the reality of what it still takes to get ahead.”

schema.headline: Hollywood Assistant Horror Novel ‘This Town Will Eat You Alive’ Written Under Pseudonym by Industry Insider Set at Hanover Square Press (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Norman Reedus Joins James Marsden in Apple TV Thriller Series ‘Disavowed’
description:
Aug 31, 2026 10:00am PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									Kevin Scanlon
	

		
	
				
	Norman Reedus is set to star alongside James Marsden
body:
Aug 31, 2026 10:00am PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									Kevin Scanlon
	

		
	
				
	Norman Reedus is set to star alongside James Marsden in the upcoming Apple TV series “Disavowed,” Variety has learned. 

	The show was originally announced back in May with Marsden in the lead role. Exact details on Reedus’ role are being kept under wraps. 

	The show is based on an original idea by Art Marcum & Matt Holloway. The logline states that it “follows legendary CIA Case Officer Brad Griffin (Marsden), who is abruptly fired in the middle of a global hunt for an elusive assassin responsible for killing his colleague. Disgraced and outcast from the world of intelligence, all bets are off when Brad decides to go after the 15 million dollar federal bounty on the assassin’s head.” 
	

	Reedus’ best known TV role is that of Daryl Dixon in “The Walking Dead” franchise. He was a main character in the mothership show for 11 seasons before leading his own spinoff, “The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon.” The fourth and final season of that show is due to debut in 2027. In film, Reedus is known for starring in features like “The Boondock Saints,” “Blade II,” “The Bikeriders,” and “Ballerina.” He has also played protagonist Sam Porter Bridges in both “Death Stranding” video games. 

	He is repped by CAA, Linden Entertainment, Narrative and Jackoway Austen. 

	Marcum and Holloway serve as executive producers in addition to creating the series. Tom Spezialy and Marsden will also executive produce. Blue Marble Pictures produces, with Theresa Kang and Caroline Garity serving as executive producers. Michelle MacLaren will direct the first two episodes and executive produce along with Michelle Hobbs under her overall deal with Apple TV. Apple Studios will also produce.


	
		More from Variety

title: The Ringer’s Sean Fennessey Criticizes His Parent Company’s Partnership With Netflix: ‘There’s an Inherent Conflict’ and ‘It Wasn’t My Decision’
description:
Some dissent in Bill Simmons’ The Ringer publishing and podcast network is airing out publicly.

	Sean Fennessey, the head of content for the Ringer
body:
Some dissent in Bill Simmons’ The Ringer publishing and podcast network is airing out publicly.

	Sean Fennessey, the head of content for the Ringer and host of the platform’s popular “The Big Picture” podcast, appeared on the podcast “Talk Easy With Sam Fragoso” on Aug. 30 and touched on several topics — including that Ringer shows like “Big Picture” have been licensed by Spotify to Netflix, despite the fact that the podcast’s participants discuss content that might appear on the streamer.
	

	“I think there’s an inherent conflict with the work that we’re doing,” he said. “I don’t think it totally makes sense for a show that’s covering films released by Netflix to be licensed nonexclusively to Netflix — but it wasn’t my decision, so we’re working within that reality.”


	Fennessey has been with Simmons’ company since it launched in 2016. The Netflix licensing deal was announced in October 2025. The Ringer is owned by Spotify, which acquired the media business in 2020 in a $250 million deal with Simmons.

	Elsewhere in the podcast, Fennessey, who was speaking alongside his “Big Picture” co-host Amanda Dobbins, was asked about Simmons’ podcast having ChatGPT as a sponsor, as well as his boss occasionally doing bits asking the AI chatbot what Roger Ebert might have thought about a movie released after his 2013 death.

	“I don’t like it. I’ve told Bill I don’t like it,” Fennessey said of the ChatGPT bits involving Ebert. “It’s not my decision. It’s something that he’s done. I think [fellow Ringer podcaster] Chris [Ryan] and I have both, when presented with ChatGPT Ebert, we’ve said ‘Eh, that’s not cool,’ you know. I wouldn’t want that done for me after I died, and I wouldn’t want to be represented in that way, and I revere Roger Ebert. I’m thinking very critically about AI and trying to not be an alarmist and trying to be thoughtful about what’s coming, while also having a clearer moral view of what it means and how it’s going to impact us.”
	

	Watch the video podcast in full below.

schema.headline: The Ringer’s Sean Fennessey Criticizes His Parent Company’s Partnership With Netflix: ‘There’s an Inherent Conflict’ and ‘It Wasn’t My Decision’

title: Sony Music Publishing, Warner Chappell Allege Anthropic Launched ‘Brazen Campaign’ to Illegally Train Claude on Copyrighted Songs in New Lawsuit
description: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music have filed a federal lawsuit against Anthropic that claimed the AI giant’s alleged theft of the comp
body:
Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music have filed a federal lawsuit against Anthropic that claimed the AI giant’s alleged theft of the companies’ intellectual property marked “a brazen campaign of illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading copyrighted works on a massive scale,” representing the latest legal salvo in the music industry‘s reckoning with the technology’s rise.

	The named defendants include Anthropic, CEO Dario Amodei and co-founder Benjamin Mann. The lawsuit, filed late Friday in the U.S. Northern District of California, alleged that Anthropic used thousands of the companies’ protected work — including songs such as Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell’s “Ain’t No Mountain High Enough“ and Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas is You,” among others cited in the 48-page suit — to train its Claude chatbot “in blatant violation of copyright law.” The suit asked the court to force Anthropic to stop the illegal training and pay statutory damages of up to $150,000 per infringing work, among other requests.
	

	“These acts separately and together inflict immense harm on Music Publishers and the songwriters they proudly represent,” the attorneys wrote on behalf of the publishing arms. “Defendants can no longer hide their extraordinary theft, and their mass infringement is now well-documented.”


	The plaintiffs are the respective publishing arms of Sony Music Entertainment and Warner Music Group. A WMG spokesperson had no additional comment, while a Sony Music spokesperson did not respond to an immediate request for comment. An Anthropic spokesperson said the case was merely “recycling allegations from cases already before the courts.”
	

	“Training generative AI models is a transformative fair use — as the court held in Bartz — and we will defend ourselves robustly,” said the spokesperson, referencing the company’s $1.5 billion settlement with authors in the copyright infringement case Bartz v. Anthropic The judge in that case ruled that, while Anthropic could train its models on copyrighted content, it couldn’t obtain that content through piracy. The lawyers in Sony and Warner’s case also worked on the authors’ case.

	Music companies have oscillated between lawsuits and licensing as they’ve navigated the rise of generative AI companies, often pursuing litigation before striking deals. The lawsuit follows lawsuits brought by a group of music publishers including Concord Music Group and Universal Music Group, a March lawsuit by BMG and, just last month, Round Hill Music against Anthropic over similar allegations of illegal scraping. Those ran parallel to lawsuits against the AI music generators Suno and Udio; WMG has settled its cases against the two generators, while Universal has struck a deal with Udio while it pursues its case against Suno. Sony Music remains in active litigation against both.

schema.headline: Sony Music Publishing, Warner Chappell Allege Anthropic Launched ‘Brazen Campaign’ to Illegally Train Claude on Copyrighted Songs in New Lawsuit

title: Cyprus Ferry Disaster Video Shows Panic Before Deadly Sinking
description:
Cyprus Ferry Disaster
                          Panic Caught on Video Before Sinking
body:
Cyprus Ferry Disaster
                          Panic Caught on Video Before Sinking

                            6:08 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Chilling video from inside a passenger ferry shows travelers scrambling for life jackets ... just moments before the vessel capsized and sank off the coast of Cyprus.
      
    
            The footage shows panic spreading as passengers hurriedly pull on life vests and prepare to abandon ship ... shortly after the ferry began taking on water Sunday.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            The vessel was carrying 267 people -- 259 passengers and eight crew members -- from Kyrenia in northern Cyprus to Taşucu, Turkey, when it ran into trouble just a few miles offshore.
      

            Authorities say the ferry began taking on water from the bow shortly after leaving port ... before eventually capsizing and sinking more than 1,600 feet beneath the surface.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            The disaster has left at least eight people dead and 18 others missing, while 241 people were rescued from the water.
      
    
            A massive search-and-rescue operation remains underway ... involving coast guard crews, military vessels, helicopters and emergency personnel from northern Cyprus and Turkey.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The ferry's captain and several crew members have been taken into custody as authorities investigate what caused the vessel to go down. A company employee has also been detained and appeared in court Monday.
      
    
            Investigators are also looking into disturbing claims from survivors ... including allegations some doors aboard the ferry were locked and that crew members ignored early warnings that the vessel was taking on water.
      
    
            Officials say the investigation will examine the ferry's seaworthiness, permits and safety measures as the desperate search for the missing continues.

                                11:20 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A massive island seemingly popped up out of nowhere in a Canadian reservoir ... only to completely vanish weeks later.
      
    
            The bizarre floating landmass was spotted in British Columbia's Williston Reservoir, where boaters noticed what looked like a full-blown island covered in trees drifting through the water.
      
    
      
      'According to estimates, it's bigger than the size of a Canadian football field and nearly the size of two NFL fields' https://t.co/zhFI83WOeu pic.twitter.com/AxulAa7qtW
              @Phil_Lewis_
          
  
    
            And this thing was huge ... roughly the size of two NFL football fields. Satellite imagery from July 21 confirmed it was real and floating about 60 miles west of the W.A.C. Bennett Dam.
      

            Then came the weird part ... by August 5, the island had disappeared from satellite images ... and the utility that manages the reservoir says it still doesn't know exactly where the island went.
      
    
            A spokesperson told CBC it may not have sunk at all, suggesting the island could've simply drifted back toward shore or into a more sheltered part of the massive reservoir.
      
    
            Officials also suggest unusually high water levels may have ripped the island loose from the shoreline ... before winds sent it drifting across the reservoir.
      
    
            So somewhere out there ... Canada's got a runaway island.
